questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic reputation

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a nice experience overall. However, it would be nice in the future if it were made possible to take graduate courses as a master student.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended the Golden Bear orientation and the online webinar.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I received all relevant information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Use Airbnb. Housing is expensive in Berkeley and I don't find Airbnb to be particularly pricy compared to other alternatives. The main advantage using Airbnb is that you are most likely not getting scammed. And there are many long-term rentals on Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is cheaper, but you would likely have to do a harder job yourself, getting to know other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fairly intuitive, but first come first serve systems are always stressful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration was based on a first come first serve purpose and was made available at a particular time. Full degree students had the opportunity to register earlier than exchange students, which made some courses unavailable for exchange students due to no free spots.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If in doubt, you could always write to the professor teaching the course. They were, in general, very responsive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the courses I had planned.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Decide early which classes to register for. But make the list fairly long, as not all classes might be available in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, the academic program was nice. However, as a master student, it is somewhat unsatisfying that one is not able to take graduate courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were easier than what I was used to from UCPH. Focus was put more on intuition than on pure math. However, I got a nice return to classes I took, especially in terms of economic intuition.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Public Economics
Topics in Economic research (seminar)
Labor Economics
Introduction to advanced programming in R

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Topics in Economic Research. 

The course is about writing a seminar. But you get feedback along the way and a structured timeline, which helps you establish the skills needed to succeed in writing longer projects. Likewise, the courses offer high-level guest lectures with exposure to cutting-edge economic research. I would definitely recommend this course for any students interested in research.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Tbh, I did not really engage in a lot of non-academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A loooot of different clubs. Many of which were pretty easy to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a recreational sports team. An easy way to meet a lot of people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a trip to Yosimite national park in your holidays. On weekends, go for a hike in the hills around Berkeley or take a trip to SF.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Americans are better than Europeans at speaking up in classes. If you are to get the most out of your classes, you have to attend office hours, which is uncommon for many Danes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The availability of the professors to discuss different questions within their field of research. Use the office hours to discuss potential future seminars or projects. They like helping students sharpen their own academic projects.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go to office-hours regularly.
2) Ask questions.
3) Enjoy the weather :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UCPH is a very high-level university. Although UC Berkley ranks higher on the international rankings, don't expect the academic level to be higher than what you are used to. If anything, expect a slightly lower academic level.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to know one of the professors very well, which was a very rewarding experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Writing the research paper in "Topics in Economic Research".

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
